challenge.exploration_summary: The baseline npm test suite passed with 1238 tests before changes. I inspected lib/response.js and the existing res.links tests, and chose res.links because it has a stable public response-helper interface with focused coverage and an obvious extension point for richer RFC-style Link header parameters.
challenge.feature_spec: res.links now accepts link descriptor objects in addition to strings, URL instances, and arrays. A descriptor may provide href or url for the target and any additional own properties are serialized as Link extension parameters. Array parameter values emit repeated parameters, true emits a flag parameter, and false/null/undefined parameters are skipped. Existing string, array, and append behavior is preserved.
challenge.feature_rationale: Link headers often need metadata such as type, title, hreflang, as, or templated. Supporting descriptors in res.links keeps this formatting logic in the response module where Link headers are already constructed, avoids manual header string assembly in applications, and remains backward compatible with the existing API.
challenge.bug_description: Link descriptor parameter values containing CR or LF are no longer escaped before being placed in the Link header. Realistic metadata such as a title sourced from user input can therefore trigger invalid header content, causing a 500 response and opening a header-injection class validation gap if the runtime or downstream handling permits it.

findings.description: The PR serialized descriptor property names directly as Link extension parameter names. A descriptor with an own key such as `title"; rel="last` would alter the generated Link header semantics by injecting additional parameter syntax instead of being rejected.

The PR's quoting helper only matched double quotes and backslashes, so CR, LF, NUL, and other control characters in descriptor parameter values stayed raw. For example, `{ href: 'https://example.test/', title: 'a\r\nX: y' }` would reach `setHeader` as an invalid header value and turn the response into a request-triggered 500.

The PR treated every object value as a descriptor but did not require `href` or `url`. Passing a plain object such as `{ title: 'missing href' }` would silently emit `<undefined>` as the Link target, producing an invalid header instead of failing clearly.

self_review.fix_explanation: Implemented the descriptor support through a shared Link formatter, validated extension parameter names as RFC token syntax before emitting them, escaped quoted parameter values including control characters, and rejected object descriptors that do not provide href or url. Added regression tests for the submitted feature behavior, URL instances, repeated and boolean parameters, invalid parameter names, control-character values, and missing descriptor targets.
